posts.title: Fresh Look
posts.author: Peter White
content: The summer solstice embodies the beginning of the most abundant time of the year, and the end of the Spring's many firsts and beginnings.

This year it also coincides with the first installment of a new schedule I plan to follow for sharing my life and my art. I have spent the Winter and Spring stockpiling and organizing all of my writing, constructing this new website, and thinking about what it is I want to get out of blogging, or otherwise sharing my work online. And through those quiet, cool weather activities I have settled on this set of desires: four major updates per year, one as each season begins, with summaries of new developments in my life, creative projects finished and ongoing, and any topics seizing my mind at the time; as well as an annual podcast, a recording of a conversation with the people closest to me. I anticipate continuing to do small updates whenever the urge strikes me, likely in the form of movie and book reviews, or select poems I've read or written, which will be found in boxes on the right side of this page (only on desktop for now, so pls check it out on your computer to see all of my hardwork!).

There is a lot to be done, but it's taken a lot to get here too. Thank you for checking out my site, and keep reading if you're interested in more updates from my life! If this is as far as you're reading now, I'll try to get you back here in the Fall where I'll have a mailing list, working catalogs of all my work, and a guestbook to sign!
A new site! And how it came to be!

I submitted my first short story to the Stevens writing contest in the Spring of 2020, and immediately wanted to keep track of my writings in a way that allowed me to easily share them. I created a Wordpress website and posted “American Icarus,” the story which won me second place, and a Kindle Fire.

motivation at that time came from budding desires to be a writer. Whatever that meant, I wanted it. Whatever that meant, quickly came to mean writing for a very small audience (or no audience at all), while I continued to pursue the more traditional path I was already on. I continued writing poetry and prose semi consistently, running my university's political opinion section in the newspaper for a few semesters, and participating in a few poetry clubs. My catalog slowly grew over these past six years, bolstered by annual writing challenges each November, and Wordpress has been good enough!

Still, it probably is good enough! But through 6 years of updating and expanding my portfolio, I continue adding new skills, crafts, and mediums to my repertoire. And that desire to become a writer, whatever that meant, transformed into becoming a craftsperson, or an engineer, or an artist! Or any word, so long as I could express myself. So, naturally, the challenge of throwing away the pre-made templates and fine tuned file management systems became more and more enticing. After working in a cabinet shop became working in my own garage, and after mending holes became sewing bags and attempts at costumes, and after pictures on my phone became starting out with a digital camera, or riding my bike became reassembling and improving that bike; it only seems right that posting on my website can now become learning HTML, CSS, and JavaScript to create and maintain that website on my own.

In my mind, this site update is another craft that felt necessary to learn, if only because I thought to try. At a time where new tools are marketed for their ability to do everything for us, I am proud to launch this site of 100% hand-drawn art and self-coded structures. And I am proud that these pages will change with the seasons and with my life! Although I've had great teachers and role models for every craft I've picked up, and no skill is learned in isolation, I am trying my best to emulate so-called self-taught, folk artists and trades people that have existed for all of time who see learning, and the imperfections that come with their 'final' products, as expression and art in themselves.
So… if you are continuing to read here, after I have come down from my soapbox, welcome!

At this moment I'm still working out how I want to organize the backend of my catalogs, for poetry, prose, photos or anything else, and so those sections are still under construction. Check back soon if you do want to take a look at any of those sections! I expect that the bulk of the formatting may continue to change, but I am happy with how it looks now, so I hope you enjoy! I began this process by looking through the amazing sites on
, and was really inspired by the user
simple but care-filled style. From their site I was pointed towards

where I was really able to get off the ground. Once I had a layout in the rough shape I wanted, it just took a few weeks of tweaking and re-tweaking, drawing and re-drawing. Feel free to look through the website's code if you'd like! It's all kept and updated via
. And if you are looking to build your own site, I can highly recommend
. It is such a satisfying experience to create something that is truly bespoke and just how you were able to make it, and if you need help I would love to offer my extremely limited knowledge.

In addition to managing my posts, Wordpress hosted my site and acted as my domain's registrar. So to make my site really my own I had to find a new host and registrar. As my self imposed deadline of the summer solstice approached, this task became a bit more daunting everyday. I'm slowly learning about the architecture of the internet, but I am happy to defer to more knowledgeable people… so recommendations from a friend resulted in free hosting through vercel (vercel.com), and my domain remains with wordpress for the time being. I'm sure these will change and be included in the next update coming in Fall, when I will have figured out what I want out of these services. Hopefully.

Again due to the self-imposed deadline, you'll notice that this is the only active page on the site, while all other links take you to the “under construction” page. I want my catalogs of work to be presentable, and those parts of the site to be interactive. For now, this is just a blog post and a pretty facade… but in the Fall you'll get to see it all! If you want to check out my work to this point, my poetry and stories are still on wordpress
The same life! And how it has developed!

The website itself has taken a lot of thought and planning, but I am most excited for the avenues it will help me create to continue my writing. I've been intimidated by the casual and genuine world of blogging, so, as this homepage shows, I'm making it a focal point! I'm looking forward to becoming more comfortable writing about my life, and for how it will integrate with my journaling practice that already has its own rhythm. Each season's change will be accompanied with a longer form, more public (kind of) meditation. And that sounds like a good time to me. So, here it is, wading in to blogging.

When I've posted my website for the world to see I will have just returned from Chicago with my partner, visiting my sister for the first time since she moved (and since I moved, actually!). We had a great time hopping between a Chicago river architecture tour, cultural festivals, the sand and concrete beaches of Lake Michigan, and the friendly confines of Wrigley Field for my first Cubs game! Go Cubs. Sorry I could not eat 9 hot dogs, I wanted it to be fun and not painful. Still, I performed better than the visiting Blue Jays…

2026 so far has been more action packed than I would've anticipated. We've traveled between NYC, New Jersey, and Virginia pretty consistently for small celebrations and periodic visits to our families. We flew to Florida for a week on the Gulf in May. We took a little road trip to the finger lakes. And we've found time to make the most of New York; going to concerts and parks, art galleries and happy hours. All that has continued on at its whirlwind pace, and now we are fully switching to packing and moving mode, as we relocate to a new place in Astoria where it's just us.

I learned from rereading my journal entries every year that I often say, surprised, that the most recent time in my life has been the best time yet. It almost makes me feel like an unreliable narrator, but I wouldn't have it any other way. 2026 has only solidified that pattern; moving in with my partner, advancing at my first permanent job, living in New York in such an important time for the city, it's all so much more than I could have imagined a year ago. While I miss home from time to time, I have never felt more surrounded by love.
Creative updates! And where it will go next!

From my other writing practices I've been learning more and more that it is a muscle you have to keep active. With more recent focus on physical crafts, it has been difficult to write this update, especially in a format I've never really tried before. When Fall comes around, my only hope is that I'll be more comfortable writing in my blog. Well… I hope I'll have a raise at work, plenty of sewing projects and new woodworking to show off, and many other blessings. But I also hope I'll be more comfortable writing in my blog! And I'm extremely thankful for anyone who read this far!

My site will keep changing, and I will aim to make it more interactive, so I can really share my creations how I've envisioned it. But for now, this is it! See you in the Fall, when the leaves begin to fall and the sky turns that deep blue to signal the coming blanket of Winter.

posts.title: Summer Slows to Fall
posts.author: Peter White
content: It’s fall, and the weather is cool. It’s fall, and the sunlight is cooler. It’s fall and it makes me wonder, has this become my favorite season? Or is there something simply irresistible and seducing in seasonal changes and cycles? It’s fall, and I’m happy to be writing updates from another glorious season and chapter in my life.
Two updates in and now I’m realizing that each update will of course describe the season that came before it. Not the season which it is titled with…

So, as I am entering the fall, I am reflecting on a pivotal summer. This was the first summer in which I did not have the chance to return home. It’s a bittersweet thought. Noticing the colors change earlier than I anticipate, and predicting the temperature of the days incorrectly are signs that my brain lies more southerly than where I reside. Such signs are also moments to recognize the new patterns which surround my senses, and so become easier to welcome.

As the bursting trees and heat that thickens the air gives way to thinning canopies and sharp, crisp mornings my website sees its construction tape slowly coming down, and I see new rhythms forming and old ones changing. My empty apartment became home, became a daily anxiety, and settled back to comfort again, before again becoming just a step toward future goals. My commute changed, and changed again without my consent. My creativity found new stages in old garments and upstate woodland gatherings. My future planning became realer than ever before. And so much more! Let’s dive in.

Firstly, I’d love to direct your attention to what’s changed on this site. My poetry catalog has revivified since leaving wordpress, and is now accessible on its own page! Please go poke through my works if you’re interested. Let me know what you think (and if it isn’t working properly), and I’ll keep making it a little easier to navigate. My writing practice has also felt fresher lately, though adding new posts to the catalog is an endeavor without professional backend management… so look out for those by the winter.

My blog catalog is also functional, and has now doubled in size! From here the next steps are more manageable: get the catalogs for my photos, prose, and physical arts up and running. A process that should take days or weeks now that the months working toward a template are complete. The goal is for all of my previous site’s functionality, and then some, to be present here by the winter. Then! More expansion, a guestbook, maybe playing with python to automatically upload poems and prose from wherever I find myself.

Before the winter I will also have a brand new part of the site dedicated to my new annual podcast! I’ve written the template, and I have my first interview set up with my partner and roommate, Sarah! I am so excited to catalog my growth through the relationships surrounding me, and to document this moment in our lives through the sounds of our voices. Stay tuned, of course.
A New Chapter in the City
After the longest day of the year the sun did not relent. It beat down for months, and is now cooling off just as the chaos of moving to a new apartment also eases.

4th of July weekend, the hottest day of the year came, followed by 3 more just as bad. And as these things often happen, it was time to move into a brand new apartment! My partner, Sarah, and I moved into our first apartment where it is just us. With the amazing help of her family and our friends David and Aaron we got a truck and got everything in (except the AC’s…) before noon on July 3rd. To continue the relaxing weekend I took the next day off unpacking and booked it down to Philly to watch France beat Paraguay in the World Cup with my brother. And on my drive back, I stopped on the RFK bridge just as it enters Astoria and watched fireworks explode just a couple dozen feet away, after being launched from the park below. To me, this weekend was when New York really began to feel like home. A new place with the person I love, non-stop work to make it livable, and an unnecessary but awesome roadtrip to see the world cup for the first time in person. Life happens where you are, and record heat can’t stop that.

From then on, the work morphed into a struggle in trying to understand how some people voluntarily live out of boxes for months while unpacking. Sarah and I enjoyed finding the best arrangements of everything in our apartment, assembling furniture and organizing. Even the IKEA shelf set that ended up taking 4+ hours to install on our plaster walls was fueled by the excitement of making something our own. Now, we don’t have any more moving expenses to shoulder and the decor is up to our standards. Maybe we’re not the best renters, but this house is a home as soon as we fill our new pitcher with fresh iced tea tonight.

On the way to the bliss of this arrangement, it wasn’t all fun and games fueled by excitement. Moving to a more accessible part of the city meant that more could go wrong too. First, just two weeks after moving in, I suffered my first (and last, please.) bike theft. The train wasn’t a bad option anymore, like in our last place, but it still gives me a twinge of sadness to think of the first bike I bought for myself. And then, just a month into the new apartment, we began seeing German cockroaches…

While we never had an infestation, and it has now been weeks without a sighting, our egos took a hit. Seeing shadows in the corners of our vision, or being scared to use the bathroom in the middle of the night because we might see evidence of imperfection in our 120 year old apartment. For me, the problem came to a head when we escaped for a weekend to the woods where Sarah is from and I felt phantom bugs on me all weekend. Being freaked out by an ant on my leg was a bridge too far. So I started spraying, and it's getting better!

Now the apartment is bug free. It’s been filled long enough to really feel like home, and to harbor creation, to let us make new places to be who we want to be. Maybe it’s just how one’s mid 20’s are supposed to go, but comfort today looks like looking ahead to see what’s next. While doing what needs to be done to live how I’d like.
And Setting up for the Future

Finally, as I have alluded to, I ended up doing a lot this summer to set myself up for future endeavors. I repeatedly found myself thinking about when I was small, and gawking at the endurance my parents showed in running a house. I would help them with groceries for an hour or so, and as soon as we got home I would eat the Wegmans pizza we picked up and take a nap on the couch. When I would wake up my mom would still be organizing the groceries into our meals for the week, and my dad would be preparing to go pick up dog poop. How did they always do the boring tasks?

Well, as I am finding out now, those things just have to be done. At least for now, while I haven’t been doing them for very long, there’s more pride than malaise about all the house work to do. More excitement for increased responsibility and freedom that will someday come with a house and future jobs. And that excitement starts where I am.

In this next season, I’ll get to visit home a bit more. For the holidays, at least. This past summer I only got to see my family a few times on action packed weekend visits to the city. While I loved sewing a costume for the New York Renaissance Faire, and attending the US Open, or the impromptu White family ping pong tournament; in the fall I will welcome weekends back in the suburbs, wrapped in Thanksgiving food comas or the quiet sleepiness between Christmas and New Years. Between trips home, I’ll be here! Taking in the city as it cools down, and the buzz of the streets shifting inside and underground.

I hope to have more exciting updates in this regard by the winter, but for now I’m excited that my house is clean. I’m excited that I set up a saving strategy to buy a house some day, and that I demystified retirement savings for myself… at least a little bit. Maybe soon there could be a new job to celebrate, or the ever clarifying vision of the future could become the present in some ways. For now, I’m happy that I’ll have this stage of life documented, and I’m happy that you got to know what I’ve been up to. If you read this far, please shoot me a text! I’d love to hear some about your summer.
